newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Detroit Diesel, Brazil state to sign plant deal.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Diesel, Brazil state to sign plant deal.

text.p: Detroit Diesel Corp and the Brazilian state of Parana will sign an accord Tuesday for the construction of a motor factory in the state capital of Curitiba, state officials said.

The state said in a statement that Detroit Diesel plans to spend at least 130 million reais ($123 million) on the plant and could invest another 90 million reais ($85 million) "in accordance with market needs."
The plant, which will build motors for cars and trucks, will create 186 jobs.
The agreement will be signed by company officials, state Gov. Jaime Lerner and Curitiba Mayor Cassio Taniguchi at 1000 local/1300 GMT at the state house, known as Iguacu Palace.
Other global carmakers already operate or have plans to build new plants in Parana.
French carmaker Renault operates an assembly plant in Parana and Volkswagen's new 500 million-real Audi plant outside Curitiba should begin production in December.
Chrysler also plans a 315 million-real factory in Campo Largo and has joined with Bayerische Motoren-Werke AG (BMW) to build a $500 million in a motor plant.
Volvo AB, which has operated in Parana for 20 years, has invested $230 million in a truck cabin factory.
